overview: A one-page confidential telegram filed under Japanese cable censorship reports that official British cables sent from Tokyo to the Pacific Coast were being held by Japanese authorities for approximately four days before transmission. Originating in San Francisco on July 15, 1941, the information was circulated within the U.S. diplomatic, military, and naval intelligence establishment shortly before the Pacific War.

people.name: Wilson
people.role: Reporting officer or sender in San Francisco; exact position not stated

subfiles.title: Telegram from Wilson on delays to British cables from Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports that Japanese authorities were delaying official British cables from Tokyo to the Pacific Coast by about four days.
subfiles.summary: Wilson relays information that official British cable traffic from Tokyo to the Pacific Coast had recently been detained for roughly four days before being forwarded. The confidential report was distributed to the State Department and senior U.S. Army and Navy intelligence and planning offices.

interest: The telegram provides concise evidence of Japanese interference with British official communications during the tense months preceding the Pacific War. Its broad distribution to diplomatic, military-intelligence, war-planning, and naval-intelligence offices shows that cable delays were treated as strategically significant. The document is useful for studying communications surveillance, censorship, and growing Anglo-American concern about Japanese policy in mid-1941.
